Open this 3D scene through a web server

This page was opened straight from a file on your computer. Browsers block map imagery and 3D models for pages opened that way, so the scene cannot draw. On the website it works as it is.

To preview it on your computer, open a terminal in the website folder (the one that holds index.html and demos) and run:

python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1

Leave that running, then open:

http://127.0.0.1:8000/demos/s3/aesa/king-farm-barn/

AESA SEARCH-WHILE-TRACK 3D STUDIO
4-Face Active Phased Array • The Barn rooftop, King Farm (Rockville, MD) • 39.12°N, 77.18°W • Non-Weaponized Observation
SCENE & LENS PREVIEW 0.0s / 60s AESA 4-FACE SWT

Each dwell's detections are drawn from its probability of detection (radar equation, beam shape, clutter), not from simulated signals. The scheduler, detector and tracker run for real on those detections.

IQ check: 12 dwells where the fidelity audit doubts the statistical model were re-run as synthesized IQ (pulses, pulse compression, Doppler FFT, CFAR). Their IQ markers show on the beam; Statistics, IQ check shows each range-Doppler map beside the statistical result.

Cued SAR: 4 confirmed ground tracks cued the site's airborne SAR (pink). Statistics, SAR chips shows each image with the track, the true position and where SAR puts the moving target.

Search beam Track beam Confirm beam Cued beam Face sector

A short-range cued EO/IR camera on the mast is slewed to confirmed tracks; whether it detects, recognises or identifies follows the Johnson criteria, drawn the same statistical way. Its picture is rendered LWIR of the scene from the mast, so it also shows what the Johnson model ignores: a roof or tree in the line of sight.

Map controls

Choose a view, then explore the map. Use Inspect for the current target or track.

Save and share

Choose an object, then click the map to place it. Cue points the radar at the active target. Python code is available for advanced editing.

Explore → inspect → compare

Play advances this exported scenario. Drag to pan or orbit; pinch or scroll to zoom. Map controls changes the camera, basemap and overlays. Inspect opens telemetry without leaving the map.

Observer camera vs. sensor pose: Orbit, Free Fly (WASD + Q/E vertical + Shift boost + mouse-look/arrows), and Street Walk (terrain eye-clamped) move only your observer viewpoint without changing the simulated radar gimbal, beam pointing, or recorded telemetry. Radar locks the viewport to the simulated sensor vantage; Target Chase follows the selected entity. Building collision push-out applies only inside modeled CAD building footprints; touch devices use standard pan/pinch/tilt without desktop pointer-lock.

Know what you are viewing

The 3D scene and EO / IR / RF lenses are display representations. They are not calibrated optical, thermal or measured radar imagery. Use the Workbench scientific evidence workspace for recorded signal products and their provenance.

Keyboard and touch

Tab moves between controls. Enter or Space activates a button. Escape closes tools and returns to the button that opened them. Panels scroll independently of the map.

Basemaps need a network connection and are subject to the provider’s terms. Exports do not add a paid map subscription or provide offline map tiles.
